turns.assessment: The alarm pattern strongly indicates a physical multi-cable break close to S20: both directions of the S20–S01 and S20–S13 links lost OSC simultaneously, with downstream amplifier input LOS. A fibre cut can affect both fibres and multiple cables in one duct, fitting this much better than a ROADM WSS fault, which should not remove OSC. However, the evidence identifies two named spans rather than one repairable element, so no single proposal reaches the commitment threshold for the cause of svc288.

proposals.rationale: OSC loss occurs on the first span leaving S20 and the corresponding reverse-direction terminal span, while the downstream inline amplifier loses input. This is the signature of both fibres of the S20–S01 cable being cut near S20.

The simultaneous OSC and signal loss in both directions on S20–S13 similarly localizes a break to the first physical span near S20. The coincidence with the S20–S01 failure suggests one excavation event affecting multiple cables.
roadm.S20 is the stated common dependency, but a WSS input-port failure does not explain OSC loss on two separate bidirectional line systems, so this is unlikely.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
